plan: Since the sealed bid acts as an exit point in a second-price-like ascending auction, the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. This ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the market price and pay only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying.

This auction structure (sealed bid as exit price in ascending clock) is equivalent to a second-price auction. In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior - it maximizes expected profit. Bidding higher risks winning and losing money if I overpay relative to my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $34, I should bid exactly $34 to ensure I only win when profitable and pay the efficient second-highest price.

Since this auction functions like a second-price (Vickrey) auction—my sealed bid sets my exit point, and I pay the second-highest bid if I win—the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $33, bidding $33 maximizes my expected profit.
